items.text: Quarterly Audit and Performance Review Report (QAPR) GM Herrera informed the Commission that Nancy Hom was selected as the AGM for Business Services. AGM Hom thanked GM for the opportunity and introduced Irella Blackwood, Audit Bureau Director who provided the QAPR. Director Blackwood indicated that for FY 2022-23 there have been 28 audits and assessments with 14% complete (4), 54% in progress (15), and 32% (9) upcoming. She stated the Calendar Year 2021 Post Audit, and the FY 2021-22 Annual Physical Inventory Count have been completed. Director Blackwood reviewed open City Services Auditor audits and recommendations and stated management agrees with the recommendations. She provided a review of FY 2022-23 fourth quarter audits that are completing and are upcoming

items.title: Lower Tuolumne River Fall-run Chinook Salmon Background and Update
items.text: Lower Tuolumne River Fall-run Chinook Salmon Background and Update Bill Sears, Science and Policy Analyst, Natural Resources and Lands Management Division, began with a review of the fall-run Chinook salmon lifecycle. He discussed “escapement” indicating it is adult fish that escape harvest and mortality to spawn in rivers. He noted it does not include escapement from hatcheries. He stated the adult escapement counting weir counts adults on their way in; Rotary Screw Traps (RSTs) estimate the number of juveniles on their way out; and the two RST locations allow estimation of juvenile survival between the two traps. Analyst Sears discussed how escapement is looking thus far and noted cumulative Chinook passage at the Tuolumne River weir (2016 through 2022). He reviewed the decline of Tuolumne fall-run over the decades (1952 through 2021) and the breakdown of the spring flow/escapement relationship (1952 to 2021). Mr. Sears reviewed contributing factors to low escapements and discussed what is being done. He indicated the Voluntary Agreement includes measures to increase in-river productivity and survival (habitat restoration, floodplain rearing flows, larger spring pulse flows to increase juvenile survival, and predation suppression to increase juvenile survival). He stated hatchery strays continue to undermine efforts to improve Tuolumne escapement. items.title: Discussion and possible action to amend Resolution No. 17-0155 to authorize the General Manager to execute an amendment to the Installment Sale Agreement and Grant State Revolving Fund loan and grant for the San Francis
items.text: Discussion and possible action to amend Resolution No. 17-0155 to authorize the General Manager to execute an amendment to the Installment Sale Agreement and Grant State Revolving Fund (SRF) loan and grant for the San Francisco Westside Recycled Water Project, increasing the not-to-exceed loan and grant amount from $186,220,000 to $191,094,031, and extending the grant agreement’s estimated construction completion date to October 7, 2024. Alexandra Gunnel, Grants and Loans Manager, introduced the item and stated it is one of nine SRF financing agreements the SFPUC has executed with the State Water Resources Control Board since 2014. She stated the SRF loan and grant offers a cost-saving alternative to revenue bond financing for water and wastewater capital projects. She indicated the original resolution for the funding agreement was approved in 2017 and since that time the project budget and duration have increased. She indicated the amendment would improve alignment between the loan agreement and the project budget and schedule

items.text: Authorize the General Manager to request Board of Supervisors approval of a supplemental appropriation ordinance in the amount of $4,579,056 for FY 22-23 to implement and administer the CleanPowerSF (CPSF) Community Food Service Energy Efficiency Program, $1,526,352 of which to be placed on Controller’s Reserve to cover the final costs of the program. items.title: Award Contract No. PW-009R, As-Needed Electrical Distribution Installation & Construction Support, in the amount of $11,500,000
items.text: Award Contract No. PW-009R, As-Needed Electrical Distribution Installation & Construction Support, in the amount of $11,500,000, and with a duration of 730 consecutive calendar days, following successful negotiations as authorized by the Commission by Resolution No. 22-0060 (March 22, 2022), to VIP Powerline Corp., in accordance with San Francisco Administrative Code Section 6.23(c)(1). The contract will augment existing Power Enterprise Field Services staff to provide services to the City’s customers, respond to emergency outages, and provide system reliability. Ramon Abueg, Deputy AGM Power Enterprise, introduced the item and discussed the work and services to be performed under the contract. He reviewed the Request-for-Proposal (RFP) process and noted there was no response to two RFP advertisements. He stated that under Resolution 22-0060, the Commission authorized the GM to negotiate a contract with a qualified contractor, as allowed under the San Francisco Administrative Code. He indicated VIP Powerline Corporation submitted a proposal that accepted all city standards, contract terms, and conditions, and that the proposal was below estimate. In response to a question from Commissioner Paulson, Deputy AGM Abueg indicated that VIP Powerline has a record of similar work and will utilize IBEW Local 1245 trained, qualified, and skilled staff to complete the work
